full_judgment:
20. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, the learned Advocate on behalf of defendants Nos.5-16 appellants of First Appeal No. 212 of 2009 submits that the root of disputes between the parties based on the deed in question being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 corresponding to 11-1-1359 BS and the agreement for reconveyance of the said land executed on the same date stipulated a period of 3 years from the said date that is to say, the time for reconveyance expired on 30th chaitra 1361 corresponding to 24-4-1956 and the said transaction is not attracted by section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. He further submits that a transaction by way of out and out sale with an separate agreement to reconvay deed was not a mortgage before coming into effect of the Presidents Order (PO 88 of 1972) read with Presidents Order 136 of 1972, because of facts such transaction was not a mortgage by definition of "Mortgage" as provided in section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act. He next submits that where the agreement to recovery is embodied in the same document by which sale is effected the transaction is conditional mortgage. He also submits that the deed in question is out and out sale with an agreement to recovery which has been treated to be mortgage under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and same was not alive on 3-8-1972, the date of coming into effect of the Presidents Order 88 of 1972. He further submits such transaction is past and closed and the property involved in such transaction will not be redeemable. He finally submits that the trial court erroneously held that the deed in question is out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey constituted a complete usufructuary mortgage for 7 years and ignoring the doctrine past and closed decreed the Title Suit No.51 of 2001 for redemption of mortgage and khas of possession in respect of 0.34 acres of suit land is totally illegal. In support of his submissions learned advocate referred the decision reported in 32 DLR(AD) 233, 16 BLD (AD) 210 = 1 BLC (AD) 90 and 1 BLC (AD) 164. 

 29. The core issue in this appeal is that whether the Deed No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 and reconveyance deed No.720 dated 24-4-1952 (Exhibit-X, X(I) are the basic documents upon which the parties claimed their respective title is complete usufructary mortgage or treated to be mortgage under section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and whether the deed in question is attracted to section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 34. In order to appreciate the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates, now we can look into the definition of "Treated to be mortgage" under section 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 50. First Appeal No. 230 of 2009 is allowed with modification that the deed in question being No. 719 dated 24-4-1952 is treated to be a mortgage but since the said deed is not alive on 3-8-1972 at the time of promulgation of Presidents Order No. 88 of 1972 is not hit under section 95A of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.
